title: Astela policies
description: A policy file of Astela on Linux, in /etc/astela/policies/managed/ for mandatory or /etc/astela/policies/recommended/ for recommended policies. Written by tools/policies/reference.ts; docs/admin/policies.md describes every policy.

ApplicationLocaleValue.description: The language of the menus, dialogs and pages of the browser: system, or a language code such as en or de. A code without a translation shows English. Unlike in Chromium, a code with a region, such as de-DE, is not valid. Takes effect after a restart.

AutoHideToolbar.description: Whether the tabs and the toolbar hide until they are needed, with the tab strip at the top and never in popups. As a mandatory policy, it also keeps the command that turns the hiding on and off from running, and the layout presets of the settings page and the setup guide that would change it cannot be chosen.

AutoUpdateCheckPeriodMinutes.description: The minutes between two automatic checks for updates. Without the policy, the browser checks every 240 minutes. Mandatory only. Takes effect after a restart.

BlockThirdPartyCookies.description: Keeps cookies away from requests, responses, frames and workers of other sites than the one of the page. Chromium blocks them from the next start of the browser, with the policies that the last start read. Private windows always block them. Takes effect after a restart.

BookmarkBarEnabled.description: Shows or hides the bookmarks bar.

CommandPaletteEnabled.description: Turns the command palette and tab search on or off. While it is off, their shortcuts reach web pages.

ContentBlockerAnnoyancesEnabled.description: Turns the optional list of the content blocker against annoyances on or off.

ContentBlockerCookieNoticesEnabled.description: Turns the optional list of the content blocker against cookie notices on or off.

ContentBlockerEnabled.description: Turns the content blocker on or off.

DefaultBrowserSettingEnabled.description: false keeps people from making the browser their default browser. The setting then says that the organization manages it, and the browser refuses the change. Mandatory only.

DefaultSearchProviderSearchURL.description: The search address of the address bar and the new tab page. An https address with %s where the search terms go, such as https://search.example.com/search?q=%s. Chrome's {searchTerms} is not supported. Mandatory only. Sensitive: applies only from managed/.

DeveloperToolsAvailability.description: 2 keeps the developer tools closed: F12, Inspect in the context menu and the menu items do nothing. 0 and 1 allow them for web pages, as in Chromium. The pages of the browser itself never get the developer tools. Mandatory only.

DnsOverHttpsMode.description: How the browser looks up the addresses of sites: automatic uses DNS over HTTPS with the services of DnsOverHttpsTemplates or, without them, where the provider of the system offers it; secure only with the services of DnsOverHttpsTemplates; off never. secure without a service works like automatic. Mandatory only. Sensitive: applies only from managed/.

DnsOverHttpsTemplates.description: The DNS over HTTPS services that DnsOverHttpsMode uses: https:// URI templates, separated by spaces. Templates that Chromium would refuse, such as ones with unbalanced braces or a variable in the host, are not valid. Mandatory only. Sensitive: applies only from managed/.

DownloadDirectory.description: The folder where downloads are saved; empty for the downloads folder of the system. Unlike in Chromium, variables such as ${user_home} are not replaced.

HomepageLocation.description: The page of the home button and of its shortcut, as an http or https address; empty for the new tab page.

HttpAllowlist.description: Hosts that HTTPS-First leaves on their insecure address, such as intranet.example.com. [*.]example.com and *.example.com also name every host below example.com. IP addresses, names without a dot and names that end in .localhost, .local, .internal, .lan, .home.arpa, .test, .example, .invalid are never upgraded and need no entry. Mandatory only.

HttpsOnlyMode.description: Whether HTTPS-First loads sites over HTTPS and warns before an insecure connection: disallowed turns it off, force_enabled and force_balanced_enabled keep it on. The browser has one mode, so both values that keep it on do the same. Chrome's allowed, which leaves the choice to people, is not valid. Mandatory only.

ImportEnabled.description: false turns off the import from other browsers, on the settings page and in the setup guide. Mandatory only.

PictureInPictureEnabled.description: Turns the picture in picture of the browser on or off: its button next to the address bar and its menu items. A video that shows in picture in picture stays there, and pages that offer picture in picture themselves keep it.

PrivateModeAvailability.description: 1 keeps people from opening private windows; 0 allows them. Chrome's 2, which makes every window private, is not supported and not valid. Mandatory only.

PromptForDownloadLocation.description: Whether the browser asks where to save each download.

ReaderViewEnabled.description: Turns the reader view on or off. While it is off, the browser checks no page for an article.

RestoreOnStartup.description: What the browser opens when it starts, with Chromium's numbers: 1 the last session, 4 the pages of RestoreOnStartupURLs, 5 a new tab page. After the browser did not quit normally, as after a crash, it brings the last session back; only a mandatory RestoreOnStartup keeps the start to its value then, as on shared computers.

RestoreOnStartupURLs.description: The pages that open at the start when RestoreOnStartup is 4, in this order.

SetupGuideEnabled.description: false keeps the setup guide from opening on the first start of a profile. Starting the browser with --no-first-run does the same for one start. Mandatory only.

ShowHomeButton.description: Shows or hides the home button of the toolbar.

SleepingTabsEnabled.description: Whether tabs go to sleep by themselves after they were not used for a while. People can still put a tab to sleep from its menu.

SleepingTabsTimeout.description: How many seconds a tab stays unused before it goes to sleep, with the values of Microsoft Edge.

SplitViewEnabled.description: Turns split view on or off. Off ends the split views that show.

SSLErrorOverrideAllowed.description: false keeps people from continuing to a site whose certificate is not trusted; certificates accepted earlier in the session are refused again. Mandatory only.

TabStripPosition.description: Where the tab strip is: at the top, at the bottom, or on the left or right side.

TargetChannel.description: The update channel. The beta channel also receives the stable releases. A switch from beta to stable never installs an older version; the browser stays on its version until a stable release overtakes it. Mandatory only. Takes effect after a restart.

TargetVersionPrefix.description: Installs only versions that start with this prefix, such as 0.1: the highest version of the feed that matches. Mandatory only. Takes effect after a restart.

ToolbarPlacement.description: Whether the address bar has a row of its own below the tabs (own-row) or shares the row of the tabs (tab-row). It applies only with the tab strip at the top.

UpdatePolicy.description: How the browser updates itself: 0 not at all, 1 by itself, 2 only when people ask for it. This version has no way to ask for an update yet, so 2 works like 0. Installations that the system or IT updates, such as the deb, rpm and MSI packages, never update themselves. Mandatory only. Takes effect after a restart.

UpdateURL.description: The address of an organization mirror of the update feed, instead of the website of the project. The browser reads updates/v1/index.json and updates/v1/releases/<version>.json below this address and checks their signatures as on the website. Mandatory only. Sensitive: applies only from managed/. Takes effect after a restart.

WorkspacesEnabled.description: Turns workspaces on or off. Off shows the tabs of all workspaces of a window together; the workspaces come back when the policy turns them on again.
